learning_objectives: Tell slowing growth apart from shrinking, and both apart from a business that is losing money.
See how a big drop can be a bargain or a trap, and why nobody knows which on the day.
Weigh debts and future spending promises against profit and coin.
Size a position when the evidence points both ways.

world.tone_notes: Moody, theatrical fantasy: dream-lanterns that show tales in every home, rival theatres rising, a guild that once seemed unstoppable. Evidence points both ways; reward careful reasoning, not hindsight. Never use real names, years, months or brands; never write amounts in prose, use the figure placeholders.

checkpoints.label: The winter scroll and a sudden fall
The first lost members in a decade
The morning of the great fall

company_card.name: The Dreamweaver Guild
company_card.trade: Rents dream-lanterns that show tales and plays in members' homes, for a fee each moon
company_card.size: The largest lantern guild of the realm, with members in almost every kingdom

key_figures.label: Paying members
key_figures.explain: Each member pays a fee every moon.

key_figures.label: Takings in the last season
key_figures.explain: Takings are fees collected before costs.

evidence.title: The winter Season Scroll
evidence.player_text: The Season Scroll shows takings of {FIG-Q4-REV} and {FIG-Q4-ADDS} new paying members this season, for {FIG-MEMBERS} in all. For the coming season the Guild expects only {FIG-Q1-GUIDE} new members, far fewer than the {FIG-Q1-PRIOR} it added in the same season a year before.

figures.label: New members in the same season a year earlier
figures.period: the same season a year earlier

evidence.teaching_note: Still growing, but the Guild itself expects much slower growth.

evidence.title: Scholar Fenwick's growth table
evidence.player_text: Scholar Odile Fenwick lines up the yearly growth in members: each year the Guild added fewer new members than the year before. In the home realms, she says, almost every household that wants a dream-lantern may already have one.
evidence.teaching_note: When a market fills up, growth slows even if nothing is wrong.

evidence.title: The first fall
evidence.player_text: The day after the winter scroll, dream-shares fell about {FIG-JAN-DROP} percent on the Moonstone Exchange.

figures.label: One-day fall of dream-shares
figures.period: the day after the winter scroll

evidence.teaching_note: A big fall shows disappointment; it does not say whether the price is now cheap.

evidence.title: Rival theatres
evidence.player_text: At the tavern, players grumble that several great houses have opened rival lantern-theatres with cheaper fees and famous old tales of their own.
evidence.teaching_note: Competition can slow growth and push up the cost of new tales.

evidence.title: What the rivals pay
evidence.player_text: A theatre carpenter tells you the rival houses are spending heavily and losing coin to win members, and some may not keep it up.
evidence.teaching_note: Rivals losing money can be a threat now and a relief later.

evidence.title: Higher fees in the home realms
evidence.player_text: The Guild has raised its monthly fee in the home realms. Traders argue whether members will pay more or leave.
evidence.teaching_note: Raising prices tests how loyal customers are.

evidence.title: The spring Season Scroll
evidence.player_text: The Guild lost {FIG-Q1-LOSS:abs} paying members this season, its first loss in more than ten years, after promising to add {FIG-Q1-GUIDE2}. Takings still rose {FIG-Q1-REV-YOY} percent to {FIG-Q1-REV}, and the Guild kept {FIG-Q1-MARGIN} percent of takings as profit from its trade. It expects to lose about {FIG-Q2-GUIDE:abs} more members next season.

figures.label: Change in paying members this season
New members the Guild had expected
Change in takings against a year earlier
Share of takings kept as trade profit
Expected change in members next season

evidence.teaching_note: Shrinking members, but still growing takings and still profitable: the evidence points both ways.

evidence.title: The shared lanterns
evidence.player_text: The Guild says its lanterns are shared with more than {FIG-SHARED} households that do not pay, {FIG-SHARED-HOME} of them in the home realms. It plans to start charging for sharing.

figures.label: Sharing households in the home realms

evidence.teaching_note: A problem can also be an opportunity: sharers might become payers, or leave.

evidence.title: Leaving the Frost Kingdom
evidence.player_text: The Guild stopped its lanterns in the Frost Kingdom during a war there, which alone cost it {FIG-FROST} members.

figures.label: Members lost by leaving the Frost Kingdom

evidence.teaching_note: Separate one-off losses from the underlying trend.

evidence.title: Coin, debts and promises
evidence.player_text: The Guild holds {FIG-CASH} in coin, owes {FIG-DEBT} in debts, and this season took in {FIG-FCF} more coin than it spent. It has promised large sums to tale-makers for years ahead.

figures.label: Coin taken in beyond spending this season

evidence.teaching_note: Debts and spending promises do not shrink when members do.

evidence.title: The Guild's new plans
evidence.player_text: Steward Lysa Corran admits the Guild is now considering a cheaper lantern that shows heralds' messages between tales, something it long refused, and charging households that share.
evidence.teaching_note: New plans can work or fail; they are not results yet.

evidence.title: The great fall
evidence.player_text: The morning after the spring scroll, dream-shares fell about {FIG-CRASH} percent in a single session. Some of the Guild's best-known backers are said to be selling.

figures.label: One-day fall of dream-shares
figures.period: the day after the spring scroll

evidence.teaching_note: A price that falls a third in a day can be a bargain or a trap; the day itself cannot tell you which.

evidence.title: A famous backer gives up
evidence.player_text: A runner whispers that a famous investment house that bought dream-shares only weeks ago has sold them all at a large loss, saying it can no longer judge the Guild's future.
evidence.teaching_note: Even experts change their minds; that is information, not proof.

evidence.title: Scholar Fenwick's two columns
evidence.player_text: Scholar Fenwick writes two columns. Known: members are shrinking, takings still grow, the Guild still makes a trade profit, it carries large debts and spending promises, and it has new plans for cheaper lanterns and sharing fees. Unknown: whether members return, whether the plans work, how hard rivals push, and whether the price has fallen too far or not far enough.
evidence.teaching_note: When evidence points both ways, size your bet for being wrong.

documents.title: Notice of the Frost Kingdom exit

characters.name: Scholar Odile Fenwick
characters.role: Keeper of the Guild's scrolls in the Library. Precise and cautious; explains both sides and never tells anyone what to buy.
never: Give an opinion on whether to buy, hold or sell
Reveal anything about prices after today

characters.name: Broker Garrick Stone
characters.role: A gruff broker on the Moonstone Exchange who reads the board and repeats what the big houses do. Gloomy after the fall.
never: Reveal anything about prices after today

characters.name: Steward Lysa Corran
characters.role: Steward of the Dreamweaver Guild's hall. Speaks for the Guild and its plans, never for the share price.
never: Promise that the plans will work

encounters.title: Slowing or Shrinking?
encounters.failure_forward: The tables are dense, but Scholar Fenwick will explain the trend if you ask.
encounters.teaching_target: Slowing growth is not the same as shrinking.

encounters.title: What the Rivals Pay
encounters.failure_forward: The carpenter clams up; the tavern still grumbles about cheaper rival theatres.
encounters.teaching_target: Competitors' costs shape how long a fight lasts.

encounters.title: The Steward's Plans
encounters.failure_forward: The steward stays guarded, but the spring scroll already mentions charging for shared lanterns.

encounters.title: The Backers' Whisper
encounters.failure_forward: The runners spot you and hurry off; the board still shows the fall.
encounters.teaching_target: What big holders do is information, not proof.

news.headline: The Dreamweaver Guild Loses Members for the First Time in a Decade
news.summary: The Guild lost {FIG-Q1-LOSS:abs} paying members after promising growth, expects to lose about {FIG-Q2-GUIDE:abs} more, and blames lanterns shared by more than {FIG-SHARED} households.

rubric.category: Separating facts from hopes and fears

board.title: The Dimming of the Dream-Lanterns
board.teaser: In Vellmoor the Dreamweaver Guild's lanterns light almost every home, until it loses members for the first time in a decade and its shares crash. Is it a bargain after the fall, or a trap that keeps falling? The evidence points both ways.
board.briefing: For years the Dreamweaver Guild's dream-lanterns seemed unstoppable. Now growth is slowing, rival theatres are rising and the Guild expects only a trickle of new members. Soon a new Season Scroll will tell whether members are still coming. Your question: after a big fall, is the Guild cheap or still too dear, and how much gold should you risk when the evidence points both ways?

questions: Which evidence said the Guild was weakening, and which said it was still strong? How did you weigh them?
Did the size of the fall make the shares cheap, or only cheaper?
How much did you commit when you were unsure, and why?
Was your result reasoning, timing or luck?

post_reveal_facts.text: In the weeks after the decision the shares fell further, then recovered part of the loss.
The Guild's next scroll showed a smaller loss of members than it had feared, and its cheaper lantern with heralds' messages launched later.

later_events.text: Netflix shares fell to about $163, roughly 28% below the decision-day close.
Netflix reported a Q2 loss of 970,000 subscribers, better than its 2 million forecast.

real_events.headline: Netflix loses 200,000 subscribers, its first loss in over a decade
real_events.text: On April 19, 2022 Netflix reported Q1 revenue of $7.87 billion (+{FIG-Q1-REV-YOY}%), a 25.1% operating margin and a loss of 200,000 subscribers, and forecast losing 2 million more in Q2.

real_events.headline: Netflix shares fall 35% in a day
